User guide

Quick start

Hymnist shows song lyrics on a projector screen and follows along as your church sings. Here is the fastest way to a Sunday-ready setup:

  1. Build your setlist. In Today’s setlist, search for a song and tap Add to setlist.
  2. Open the projector screen. Tap Open projector, drag the new window onto the projector, and click it once for full screen.
  3. Start the music. Tap the microphone and let Hymnist follow the singing, or tap Next line yourself. You are always in control.
Everything you change is saved on your device automatically. Nothing is lost if you close the page.

The Operator screen

This is the control center, used by the person running the lyrics. The three tabs at the top switch between Operator, Musicians and Projector.

  1. 1Preview: exactly what the congregation will see.
  2. 2Next line (and Back, Blank, Prayer beside it). Blank hides the words; Prayer shows your prayer message.
  3. 3Open projector opens the congregation screen in its own window.
  4. 4Full screen hides everything except the preview, the buttons and the Listen panel.
  5. 5Connected screens: shows how many projectors and musicians are following you. Tap it to see their names.
  6. 6Microphone: tap to let Hymnist listen and advance the lyrics for you.
  7. 7Print chord sheets (printer): make a printable or PDF sheet of this setlist.
  8. 8Plan ahead (calendar): create setlists for upcoming services.
  9. 9Song library (books): find, edit and add songs.

Listen: hands-free lyrics

Hymnist listens to the singing, finds the matching line in your setlist, and moves the screen to it.

  1. 1Tap the microphone to start or stop listening. The first time, allow microphone access when your device asks.
  2. 2No microphone? Type words as if they were sung and Hymnist reacts the same way. This is also a great way to practice.
  3. 3What it heard is shown here, so you can see what the app is working with.
  4. 4Match meter: the fuller the bar, the more confident the match.
It only matches against your setlist, so songs you did not add cannot pop up by mistake. The Next line and Back buttons always override the microphone.

If speech recognition is unreliable on a device, open Settings → Speech recognition and try Always on-device. It is slower, but it never sends audio anywhere.

Building a setlist

The Today’s setlist card is the list of songs for this service.

  1. 1Search for a song by title. Small typos are fine. Press Enter to add the first result.
  2. 2Add to setlist adds the song to the end of the list.
  3. 3Use the arrows to reorder songs and × to remove one from the setlist (it stays in your library).

A 🎸 icon next to a title means the song has chords. A ⚠ needs lyrics tag means it has no lyrics yet, so add some in the library before using it.

Printing chord sheets

Tap the printer button next to the setlist title to make a sheet of the whole setlist for the band, the choir or your own binder.

  1. 1Show, Text size and Columns: choose Chords and lyrics or Lyrics only, a small, medium or large size, and one or two columns.
  2. 2Use each song’s saved key shift and capo: prints each song the way you set it up in the editor, with a line such as “Key A · Capo 2 (play G shapes)”. Two more tick boxes add guitar chord shapes under each title and start each song on a new page.
  3. 3Print / Save as PDF opens your device’s print window. Choose “Save as PDF” as the printer to make a file.
  4. 4Download page saves the sheet as a web page you can open and print later, or send to someone.
  5. 5Copy as text copies plain text with the chords above the words, ready to paste into a message or document.
  6. 6A preview of the sheet. What you see here is what prints.
If your device cannot open a print window (some app wrappers cannot), use Download page or Copy as text instead. Your choices are remembered on that device.

Song library and adding songs

Tap the books icon to open every song you have.

  1. 1Add a song (the + button).
  2. 2Search all songs.
  3. 3Edit changes the title, lyrics or chords. Add lyrics appears for songs that have none.
  4. 4Add puts the song in the setlist you are working on.

Adding a song

  1. 1Type the title.
  2. 2Paste the lyrics. To add chords, put them in square brackets right before the word where the chord changes, like [G]Amazing [C]grace.
  3. 3Key shift and Capo are what musicians open this song with. For example, set a key shift of +2 and capo 2 for a song written in G that your singer sings in A: guitarists then play G shapes. Players can still change it for themselves.
  4. 4Tap Tidy up lyrics. It splits the song into lines, removes labels like “Verse 1”, and expands the chorus. Undo tidy brings back what you pasted.
  5. 5Add section labels adds lines like {Verse 1} and {Chorus} so the operator and musicians can see the structure.
  6. 6Repeat the chorus after each verse puts the chorus lines after every verse, so the screen never runs out of words.
  7. 7Split lines longer than breaks long lines at a comma or a space so they fit the projector. Chords stay with their words.
  8. 8Tap Save song. It is added to the library and to your current setlist.

For best results, separate verses with a blank line and put a line such as Chorus (or Refrain) above the chorus. If the chorus is only written once, later lines that just say “Chorus” are filled in for you. Bridges stay where you put them.

Only add lyrics your church is licensed to display. Hymnist does not provide or license songs. The built-in hymns are believed to be public domain in the United States.

Scripture and announcement slides

Not everything in a service is a song. In the Song library, tap + and change Type to Scripture reading or Announcement. Slides go into your setlist and move with Next line like any song, and they show on the projector in the same style.

For a Scripture reading, pick a passage from Insert a passage (KJV) or type or paste your own. The built-in passages are the King James Version, which is in the public domain; if you paste another translation, make sure you have the right to display it. For an Announcement, give it a heading and write one line per projector line. Slides are marked with a 📖 or 📢 in lists, have no chords, and are left out of printed chord sheets.

Sections: verse, chorus, bridge

Songs can have named sections. They help the operator see what is coming and help the band know where they are.

  1. 1The current section, such as Verse 1 or Chorus.
  2. 2How far you are into it, and what comes next, such as “Next: Chorus (after this line)”. On the last section it names the next song in your setlist.
  1. 1Musicians see a small section label above the first line of each section.

The projector screen never shows section labels, so the congregation only sees the words.

Adding labels to your own songs

In the song editor, a label is a line of its own in curly braces, like {Verse 1} or {Chorus}, placed above the first line of that section. The easiest way is Tidy up lyrics with Add section labels ticked: it reads “Verse”, “Chorus” and “Bridge” headings in what you pasted and adds the labels for you. You can edit or delete any label by hand. The built-in hymns already have labels.

Planning ahead

Tap the calendar icon to build setlists for upcoming services and pick the one you want to run.

  1. 1Songs: choose and reorder the songs in that setlist.
  2. 2Open: make it the active setlist on the Operator screen.
  3. 3Edit: rename it or change its date and time.
  4. 4Give a new setlist a name, plus an optional date and time.

A setlist with a date and time switches on by itself when its start time arrives, so Sunday morning is ready without anyone clicking. Leave the date blank for an always-available setlist, such as a quick list for rehearsal. Past services are kept under Show past setlists.

The projector screen

The projector screen shows only the lyrics, large, with the background you chose.

  1. Tap Open projector on the Operator screen. A new window opens.
  2. Drag that window onto the projector or second display.
  3. Click inside it once to make it full screen. Press Esc to leave full screen.

It follows the Operator screen automatically, including Blank and Prayer. If your browser blocks the pop-up, allow pop-ups for this page, or open the app in a second tab with #display added to the end of the address.

Other devices: the projector window normally needs to be on the same computer and browser as the operator. If Settings → Sync status says you are connected, other devices follow the operator automatically.

Lower third and confidence monitor

A projector window can show more than full-screen lyrics. Move the mouse over it and use the menu at the bottom right to pick Lyrics (full screen), Lower third, Lower third on green or Confidence monitor. In Settings → Extra screens, the Open lower-third window and Open confidence monitor buttons open a window already set up that way.

A lower third shows only the current line in a dark bar at the bottom, with a see-through background for a video stream. In OBS, add the window as a Window Capture, or use the green version with a chroma-key filter. A confidence monitor is for the singers: a very large current line, the next line in gold, the section and song title at the top, and the next song’s name on the last line. It keeps showing the words when the main screen is Blank or Prayer and says so at the top. Each window remembers its own choice, so you can run the main projector, a lower third and a confidence monitor at the same time.

Backgrounds for a song or a section

Besides the projector background in Settings, any song or slide can have its own. Open it in the Song library (Edit) and choose Projector background for this item: a preset, or Custom color. Songs with section labels can also have a different background for the chorus and bridge, which switches automatically when the lyrics reach those sections. Leave a choice on Same as the projector setting to use the Settings background. Photos can still be used as the main Settings background, but not per song.

Fades

In Settings, Fade between lines and backgrounds can be Off, Soft (the default) or Slow. Lines fade in and backgrounds cross-fade when they change. If a device is set to reduce motion, the fades are skipped.

Full-screen operator mode

Tap the full screen button next to the main buttons to hide everything except what you need while leading.

  1. 1The Listen panel stays at the bottom so you can see what the app is hearing.
  2. 2Tap the same button again (it now shows the exit icon) to return.

Connected screens and names

Hymnist can show who is connected, so everyone can be sure they are following the right operator.

  1. 1The status pill shows how many projectors and musicians are connected. A green dot means at least one is. Tap it to open the list.
  2. 2Each projector is listed with its name.
  3. 3Each musician is listed with their name and instrument.

Projector and Musicians screens show a pill too: Connected to operator name in green, Waiting for the operator while searching, and Lost connection if the operator goes away. If two operators are found at once, a warning lists them so you can check you picked the right one.

Setting names

  1. On the Operator screen, open Settings → Connections and type an Operator name, such as “Main Sanctuary”.
  2. On each projector or musician device, open Settings (or the Musicians gear) and type This device’s name, such as “Back wall” or “Sarah (keys)”.
Other devices. In the Claude-hosted version, screens on other devices appear in the operator’s list automatically, and each shows the operator it follows. Elsewhere (a web page link or the Android app), only windows in the same browser on the same computer can see each other.

Musicians view

Tap Musicians to see the current song with chords for your instrument. The highlighted line follows the Operator screen.

  1. 1Connection status: shows which operator you are following. Green means connected.
  2. 2Instrument: Guitar shows chord shapes, Piano / Keys shows the notes, Bass shows root notes, Vocals shows lyrics only.
  3. 3Key: the − and + buttons move the song down or up one half step at a time. It shows the key you are playing in, and how far you have moved.
  4. 4Capo (guitar only): choose the capo fret. The chord shapes shown change to match, so you play what is on the screen.
  5. 5Song default: appears when you have changed the key or capo. Tap it to go back to what the operator saved for this song.
  6. 6Text size: A− and A+ make everything smaller or larger.
  7. 7Musician settings (gear): choose a font, a text size, how the screen follows the operator, and this device’s name.

These choices are saved on each device, so every player can set the screen the way they like without changing anyone else’s. Key and capo changes are remembered per song on your device, and each new song starts with the key and capo the operator saved for it.

Notes from the operator

If the operator added a note to a song, such as “Slow intro” or “Repeat the last chorus”, it appears in a highlighted card above the chart while that song is live. Notes go to the band only and are never shown on the projector. The operator adds them in the song’s Add / Edit form under Notes for musicians and also sees the note under the stage while the song is live.

Following the operator

The chart scrolls by itself to keep the current line in view. If you scroll by hand, for example to read ahead, it pauses and a Paused · tap to follow button appears.

  1. 1Tap Paused · tap to follow to jump back to the current line. By default it also resumes by itself after 20 seconds, and always when the operator moves to a new song.
  2. 2The highlighted current line keeps moving even while the chart is paused.

Open the gear and use Follow the operator to choose: scroll along and pause when I scroll (default), pause until I tap Follow, or never scroll for me. Keep the current line chooses the middle of the screen or near the top, which shows more of what is coming.

Remote control

A second person, such as a pastor or a volunteer, can move the lyrics from their own phone while the operator keeps control of the setup.

Turn it on (operator)

  1. Open Settings → Connections and tick Allow remote control from another device.
  2. A four-digit Remote code appears. Tell it to the person who will use the remote. New code changes it at any time.

Use it (the other device)

  1. 1Shows which operator you are connected to.
  2. 2Type the remote code. It is remembered on that device. The status line tells you if the code is wrong or remote control is off.
  3. 3The current line, the next line and the section, so you can see where the song is.
  4. 4Next line, a very large button you can tap without looking.
  5. 5Back, Blank and Prayer, which light up while they are on.
  6. 6The Songs list: tap a song to jump to it.
Safety. The operator only obeys the remote while the setting is on and the code matches. After five wrong codes it pauses for 30 seconds. The operator screen shows “Remote (name): Next line.” each time, and the connected-screens list shows how many remotes are connected.
Which devices can connect? In the Claude-hosted version, remotes work from other devices. Elsewhere (a web page link or the Android app), a remote only works in another tab or window of the same browser on the same computer.

Settings

Tap the gear at the top right of the Operator screen to open Settings.

  1. 1User guide: this guide.
  2. 2Lyrics font: pick the font for the projector screen. A preview is shown below it.
  3. 3Projector lyrics size: make the words larger or smaller.
  4. 4Background: choose a preset, any custom color, or your own picture.
  5. 5Prayer message: the words shown when you tap Prayer.
  6. 6Operator name: shown on projector and musician screens.
  7. 7This device’s name: shown to the operator.

Under Connections you can also turn on remote control (see Remote control). Further down you will also find Speech recognition options, the Sync status, and the Legal notice & terms of use.

Some fonts load from the internet. If a device is offline it will show a similar built-in font instead.

Backup and moving songs

Your songs and setlists live in the browser on each device, so it is a good idea to save a copy now and then. Find these in Settings → Backup & transfer.

  1. Export backup saves a file with all your songs and setlists. If your device cannot save a file, use Copy backup text and paste it into a note or email to yourself.
  2. Import backup (or Paste backup text) reads a backup from another device. Hymnist shows you what it found before changing anything.
  3. Choose Add to my library to keep everything you have and add what is missing, or Replace everything to make this device match the backup.
Safe to try. Songs that already exist are skipped, and a song with the same ID but different words is added as a copy marked “imported”. Right after an import, Undo last import puts everything back. Display settings, fonts and names are not part of a backup.

Shortcuts and troubleshooting

Keyboard shortcuts (Operator screen)

  • → or Space Next line
  • ← Back
  • B Blank the screen
  • Enter in the search box adds the first match
  • Esc closes a window

Something not working?

“Mic error: not-allowed”
Microphone access is blocked. In a browser, tap the lock or settings icon next to the web address and set Microphone to Allow, then reload. In an installed app, open the phone’s Settings → Apps → Hymnist → Permissions and allow Microphone. If the app has no microphone option there, it was built without microphone access. Typing words into the Listen box still works.
The words don’t advance
Check that the song is in today’s setlist and has lyrics. Hymnist only matches songs in the setlist. You can always use Next line.
The projector window won’t open
Allow pop-ups for this page, or open a second tab with #display on the end of the address.
My songs and settings disappeared
They are stored in the browser on that device. Clearing the browser’s site data, or switching to a different browser or device, starts fresh.
Chords look wrong
The chords on the built-in hymns are simple, standard arrangements. Edit the song in the library to change them.
